newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money inactive on reporting day.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money inactive on reporting day.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted in the 0.10-0.50 percent range early on the reporting Friday and dealers said they did not expect any trade during the day.
Banks report their positions to the Reserve Bank of India on alternate Fridays and do not normally borrow on such days as it increases their reserve requirements for the next fortnight.
Dealers said they expected trade in government securities to be brisk. "There is good buying interest from banks for securities with maturities up to 1999," said a dealer.
"There is also demand for longer-dated securities from provident funds. With cash reserve ratio (CRR) being cut tomorrow, the increase in liquidity can be expected to boost trade further," he added.
The Reserve Bank of India last week announced a cut in banks' CRR to 10.5 percent from 11 percent, effective January 4.
